Real fact 🧊 Ice floats because it's about 9% less dense than liquid water, so lakes freeze from the top and fish survive under it.

In the sinking-ice world, would YOU live near a lake? 🅰️ Yes  🅱️ No way 👇

Honest question 👀 In a world where nobody can lie, what would you miss MORE?
🅰️ Surprise parties
🅱️ Polite little white lies
Comment A or B 👇 (and be honest 😄)

Real fact 🤖 In a 1999 UCL study, adding a 0.2 s delay through a robot made people's own touch feel about as tickly as someone else's!

Which world do you pick? 🅰️ Our world  🅱️ Delay world 👇
Fair answer! 😄 And time really does depend on height: in 2010, atomic clocks at NIST measured it tick faster when raised just 33 cm.

Real fact 🧠 In mouse studies, the spaces between brain cells grew about 60% during sleep, so the brain's 'night cleaning crew' could wash waste away faster!

Would you trade sleep for 8 extra hours a day? 🅰️ Keep my sleep  🅱️ Never sleep 👇

jobs.title: Do Cats ALWAYS Land on Their Feet? 🌀 #Swirlverse
jobs.description:
Do cats always land on their feet? Almost! A falling cat bends in the middle, tucks its front paws, spins its front half, then swaps and spins the back half. But in this parallel world, cats can't bend... 🐱
Bendy cats or stiff cats? Comment below 👇

Real science: the cat righting reflex. The front and back halves turn in opposite directions, so the total spin (angular momentum) stays zero. It needs a super flexible spine. It isn't guaranteed: a very short drop is too quick to turn. Sources: Scientific American, Live Science.

#shorts #science #cats #physics #animals #swirlverse

how cats land on their feet
jobs.first_comment:
Real fact 🐱 A falling cat spins its front half one way and its back half a little the other way, so its total spin stays zero, and it still ends up feet down!

Which world do you pick? 🅰️ Bendy cats  🅱️ Stiff cats 👇
